Friday, October 16

Game recap

BUF5TOR4OTFinal: BUF 5, TOR 4 OT

Toronto led 4-2 after 40 minutes in its own building, which, if you've followed this franchise, is not the same thing as winning. Kirill Marchenko scored a hat trick, one on the power play, and Auston Matthews scored 2:24 in, so the Leafs did their part for two periods. Then Buffalo took the third: Dennis Gilbert and Mattias Samuelsson scored 2:11 apart, and Owen Power won it 3:14 into overtime. Jack Quinn had the full evening: two goals, two assists and a second-period fight with Troy Stecher. Neither goalie will frame this one: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 26 of 30, Sergei Bobrovsky 29 of 34. Gavin McKenna played 6:36 and watched the last 33 minutes from the bench. Toronto is 3-3-2, and blowing a two-goal third-period lead at home to the Sabres is the kind of thing Leafs fans stopped calling a surprise years ago.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI1OTT2SOFinal: NYI 1, OTT 2 SO

Two teams combined for 40 shots and two goals in 65 minutes, so naturally it took a skills competition to settle it. Matias Maccelli gave the Islanders the lead with 12 seconds left in the first, unassisted, and Ridly Greig tied it late in the second with his first of the season. After that, Linus Ullmark (20 saves on 21 shots) and Semyon Varlamov (18 on 19) took turns making everyone else look silly. The first four shooters in the shootout came up empty before Shane Pinto scored in the third round, and Simon Holmstrom missed to end it. The Senators are 6-2 with 12 points. The Islanders are 3-3-1, and their offense went quiet after the first intermission and never came back, like a fan base that's been waiting since 1983.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3TBL4OTFinal: SEA 3, TBL 4 OT

Seattle came into Tampa on a three-game road win streak and left with a point and a long flight home. Ryan Winterton opened the scoring, Brandon Hagel answered with two goals for the Lightning, and the lead changed hands until Matty Beniers tied it 3-3 with 4:19 left in regulation. Jared McCann had the Kraken's power-play goal in between, and Ilya Mikheyev's unassisted goal had put Tampa back in front. Then Victor Hedman scored his first of the season 2:07 into overtime off a Pontus Holmberg feed, because of course the old man was the one who jumped into the play. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 24 of 27; Philipp Grubauer stopped 31 of 35. The Lightning are 5-2. The Kraken are 5-2-1 and got outshot 35-27, the hockey version of a Florida beach day in October: you still get burned.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2FLA3OTFinal: VAN 2, FLA 3 OT

Vancouver led 2-0 for more than 40 minutes, had Leevi Meriläinen stopping everything, and was 13 seconds from ending its losing streak. Then Brady Tkachuk happened. He cut it to 2-1 at 11:11 of the third, tied it with 13 seconds left and the goalie pulled, and won it 2:23 into overtime off Seth Jones and Sam Reinhart. Natural hat trick, all after the second intermission. Liam Ohgren and Elias Pettersson scored for the Canucks, Pettersson off a feed from Filip Chytil in his season debut. Meriläinen made 36 saves on 39 shots; Akira Schmid needed only 15 on 17 at the other end. Florida is 4-2-2. The Canucks are 2-6-1 with six straight losses, and blowing a two-goal lead with 13 seconds left is how a road trip turns into a support group.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR1NJD7Final: NYR 1, NJD 7

The Rangers walked into Newark at 6-2 and walked out with a 7-1 souvenir. Evan Rodrigues scored with 30 seconds left in the first, and then the second period turned into a fire drill: Luke Hughes, Nico Hischier and Arseny Gritsyuk scored in the first 4:39, and Dylan Garand was pulled after four goals on 13 shots. Spencer Martin came on, and Hughes beat him too for his second of the night. Stefan Noesen and a shorthanded Cody Glass piled on in the third, with Pavel Dorofeyev's power-play goal the Rangers' only reply. Nico Daws stopped 18 of 19. Will Cuylle and Johnathan Kovacevic fought in the first, and Alexis Lafrenière got a misconduct in the third, which at least got him out of the building early. The Devils are 4-3. The Rangers are 6-3, and that shiny goal difference just took a six-goal haircut.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI1DET2Final: PHI 1, DET 2

The Flyers scored first, which at this point is just how they set up the punchline. Matvei Michkov went in alone late in the first, unassisted, and Daniil Tarasov didn't allow anything else on 18 shots. Detroit tied it early in the second when Anton Johansson scored his first of the season, set up by Dylan Larkin, and Andrew Copp won it with 4:38 left, also his first. Joseph Woll was good for Philadelphia, 24 saves on 26 shots, and it bought him nothing. The Red Wings are 2-3-2. The Flyers are 0-6-3 with 11 goals in nine games, and the only thing they've won all season is the race to the bottom of the standings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG3CHI4OTFinal: WPG 3, CHI 4 OT

Connor Bedard scored his first goal of the season on a first-period power play, and the Blackhawks spent the rest of the night making sure it wasn't wasted. Frank Nazar and Ryan Donato made it 3-1 inside 18 minutes, but Winnipeg chipped back: Neal Pionk scored one and set up two more, Kyle Connor got his eighth on the power play, and Alex Iafallo tied it early in the third. Then Artyom Levshunov, from Bedard and Patrick Kane, scored his first of the season 1:37 into overtime. Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34; Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 28. Chicago is 3-5. The Jets are 4-1-2 and got a point, but every night they give up four is another reminder of who isn't in their crease.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3NSH2SOFinal: SJS 3, NSH 2 SO

San Jose was one second away from its first regulation win of the season. One. Mason Marchment and Will Smith had the Sharks up 2-0 into the third, Ryan O'Reilly got one back on the power play, and Steven Stamkos tied it with the goalie pulled at 19:59. So off to extra time, again, and a shootout, where Macklin Celebrini scored and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped Ryan O'Reilly, Filip Forsberg and Ross Colton. Nedeljkovic made 32 saves on 34 shots, Juuse Saros 30 on 32. Nicolas Hague and Zack Ostapchuk fought 2:51 in. The Sharks are 4-3, and all four wins needed more than 60 minutes. Nashville is 2-2-3: seven games, two wins, and a team that has mastered every part of hockey except the part where you win.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4MIN5Final: STL 4, MIN 5

Matt Boldy scored a hat trick, and the Wild still spent the last minute hanging on. Jonatan Berggren gave St. Louis a power-play lead 1:45 in, and then Minnesota took over: Boldy on the power play, Danila Yurov, then Boldy, Kirill Kaprizov (his ninth) and Boldy again in the second for a 5-2 lead. Quinn Hughes had two assists. The Blues made it close late: Robert Thomas scored shorthanded with four minutes left, and Dylan Holloway made it 5-4 with 15 seconds left and the goalie pulled. Jesper Wallstedt held on with 21 saves on 25 shots, and Joel Hofer stopped 33 of 38. Minnesota is 5-2-1. St. Louis is 3-3-1 and showed up about 40 minutes late, which is fashionable at a party and fatal in Saint Paul.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA4EDM2Final: UTA 4, EDM 2

Edmonton's five-game win streak ended at home, and Utah did it with special teams. Barrett Hayton and Clayton Keller scored on power plays, Logan Cooley made it 3-1 just 23 seconds after Leon Draisaitl had cut it to 2-1 (from Connor McDavid, naturally), and Keller added an empty-netter with 28 seconds left. Shakir Mukhamadullin had given the Oilers hope early in the third with an extra attacker on. Karel Vejmelka stopped 22 of 24, and Devon Levi stopped 20 of 23. Utah is 6-2 with 12 points. The Oilers are 5-1-1, and a loss in October is fine in Edmonton; it's the ones in June that keep the whole city up at night.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY2VGK6Final: CGY 2, VGK 6

Brett Howden scored 25 seconds in, and the Flames spent the rest of the night chasing a game that had already left the building. Jack Eichel added a shorthanded goal, Braeden Bowman scored on the power play, and then Mark Stone took over the third: three goals, the last on the power play, for a hat trick. Ivan Barbashev had three assists, Eichel and Mitch Marner two each. Jake Middleton scored shorthanded and Matt Coronato added a late power-play goal for Calgary. Carter Hart stopped 28 of 30, and Dustin Wolf faced 33 shots and stopped 27. Vegas is 7-2 with 14 points. The Flames are 1-6, and Vegas showed them the kind of hospitality the Strip saves for tourists who bet on the wrong team.

Thursday, October 15

Game recap

MTL4WSH5Final: MTL 4, WSH 5

Nine goals, three ties and one Alex Tuch, who decided Washington's 5-4 win over Montreal was his personal project. Tuch scored shorthanded and unassisted at 6:16 of the second to give the Capitals their first lead, 3-2, then added another unassisted goal at 17:05 of the third for a 5-3 cushion he'd need. Josh Anderson scored twice for Montreal, both set up by Alex Newhook, and Lane Hutson had a goal and an assist, but the Canadiens never led after the first period. Justin Holl, of all people, scored the winner at 12:29 of the third. Nick Suzuki made it interesting with a 6-on-5 power-play goal at 18:21, and that was as close as it got. Charlie Lindgren stopped 26 of 30; Jakub Dobes saw 23 shots and let in five. Montreal falls to 3-3-1, Washington climbs to 4-3. Two straight shootout wins had the Habs feeling clutch; turns out you can't buy a skills competition in regulation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL3COL2SOFinal: DAL 3, COL 2 SO

Colorado won the first half of this back-to-back 3-2 in Dallas on Tuesday. Dallas flew to Denver and returned the exact score, plus a shootout, for the full refund. Gabriel Landeskog opened it in the second off a Nazem Kadri feed, Miro Heiskanen answered late in the period in a 30-minute shift at the office, and Arttu Hyry scored shorthanded 1:20 into the third for his first of the season. Brock Nelson tied it at 8:21 and that was the last anybody would score with a goalie in the way. In the shootout, Jason Robertson and Roope Hintz beat Scott Wedgewood, Kadri answered once, and Nathan MacKinnon, Martin Necas and Nelson all came up empty. Casey DeSmith stopped 25 of 27, Wedgewood 20 of 22. Dallas gets to 3-3-1; Colorado is 4-2-1. Cale Makar came back for this one, and the Avs still went 1-for-4 against Casey DeSmith in the shootout, which is a sentence that should cost somebody dessert.

NHLPA executive director Marty Walsh answered Gary Bettman's concern about players using no-trade and no-movement clauses to steer trades: the clauses are the players' right, he hasn't discussed it with Bettman, and one offseason shouldn't prompt rule changes. The Athletic's James Mirtle counts 320 players with some trade protection and expects it in the 2030 CBA talks.

spectorshockey.net ↗
NYI
Lineup

Maccelli moves up to the Islanders' top line with Palmieri and Horvat; Heineman drops to the fourth

In the third period of Tuesday's 3-2 win over Vancouver, the Islanders put Matias Maccelli beside Kyle Palmieri and Bo Horvat and moved Emil Heineman to the fourth line with Simon Holmstrom and Casey Cizikas. Lineup news is expected after Thursday's morning skate in Ottawa.

nhl.com ↗
TOR
Lineup

Leafs reshuffle the top six after the loss in Utah: Nylander up with Matthews and Roslovic

Nylander moves to the top line and Nick Paul to the second with Tavares and Marchenko. Zack MacEwen could play after six straight healthy scratches, though Hiller is still weighing the 11-forward, seven-defenseman setup of the last two games.

nhl.com ↗
NSH
Lineup

Brunette goes back to 12 forwards and six defensemen against the Sharks; Bourque a game-time decision

Andrew Brunette said Nashville will dress 12 forwards and six defensemen after going 11 and 7 on Tuesday, with Jayden Struble expected in and Jack Ahcan out. Mavrik Bourque practiced and is a game-time decision; Juuse Saros was first off the ice at the optional skate.

heavy.com ↗
STL
Lineup

Pavel Buchnevich goes home to St. Louis for the birth of his child and isn't expected to play in Minnesota

The Blues say Buchnevich has returned to St. Louis for the birth of his child, isn't expected to play tonight, and that they'll update his status later. He had three assists in Tuesday's 7-2 win in Ottawa.

nhl.com ↗
TBL
Lineup

Cooper confirms Dominic James and Emil Lilleberg play against Seattle; Goncalves and D'Astous come out

Jon Cooper said James, back from a broken hand, and Lilleberg play against the Kraken, with Gage Goncalves and Charle-Edouard D'Astous out. Tampa Bay sticks with 11 forwards and seven defensemen; James centered Conor Geekie and Jeffrey Viel at the morning skate.

boltsbythebay.com ↗
NJD
Lineup

Update: Keefe says Dillon sits again as a numbers game; Devils keep the lineup that won in Detroit

Brenden Dillon is scratched again against the Rangers; Keefe said that with Kovacevic back, Dillon is the one who comes out. Declan Chisholm stays in on the third pair and the Devils use the lineup from their overtime win in Detroit.

nhl.com ↗
STL
Lineup

Pavel Buchnevich leaves the team for the birth of his child before the Blues visit Minnesota

GM Alexander Steen announced that Buchnevich has gone back to St. Louis for the birth of his child. The team gave no timing for his return and said it will update his status when it can.

nhl.com ↗
LAK
Lineup

Kings shuffle lines at practice: Laferriere joins Panarin and Kempe, Byfield moves to the second line

Thursday's lines were Panarin-Laferriere-Kempe and Moore-Byfield-Haula, with Zuccarello an extra in a full-contact jersey. Laviolette wants more offence and said the lines could change again before Saturday against Boston.

lakingsinsider.com ↗
NYR
Lineup

Lafreniere tossed with a misconduct for abusing officials in the 7-1 loss in New Jersey; Rempe scratched again

Alexis Lafreniere got a 10-minute misconduct for abuse of officials in the third period, which ended his night. Matt Rempe was a healthy scratch, Justin Dowling made his season debut and Cole Beaudoin went back to Hartford.

Confirmed · Oct 15: The NHL's game sheet shows Lafreniere's 10-minute misconduct in the third period and Rempe out of the Rangers' lineup. nhl.com ↗

Lineup

Penguins shuffle the bottom six: Robertson up to the third line, Soderblom draws in

At Thursday's practice Nicholas Robertson moved up to skate with Andrei Kuzmenko and Ben Kindel, Elmer Soderblom joined Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte, and Ville Koivunen wasn't on the four lines.

NHL.com's projected lineup for the Flyers game has Danielson on the top line with Dylan Larkin and Viktor Arvidsson, and Raymond on the third with Michael Rasmussen and Andrew Copp. Detroit held an optional morning skate.

Penguins shuffle the power play at practice: Kindel joins PP1, Rust moves to PP2

Ben Kindel joined Karlsson, Crosby, Malkin and Rakell on the top unit, and Rust worked with Letang, Kuzmenko and Chinakhov. The power play is 0-for-16 since its first two games.

Waivers

Update: Alex Barre-Boulet clears waivers and is expected to join the AHL Barracuda

Elliotte Friedman reported that Barre-Boulet cleared waivers a day after the Sharks activated him from injured reserve and put him on the wire. He is expected to be assigned to the AHL's San Jose Barracuda.

Confirmed · Oct 15: The Sharks reassigned Barre-Boulet to the Barracuda along with Cam Lund. prohockeyrumors.com ↗

VAN
WaiversNot confirmed by the team

Update: Aatu Raty clears waivers and is expected to go to AHL Abbotsford

Elliotte Friedman reported that Raty cleared waivers on Thursday. Vancouver is expected to assign him to Abbotsford, which opens the spot to activate Filip Chytil.

prohockeyrumors.com ↗

Correction · Oct 15: Raty cleared waivers but was traded to Toronto for Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr instead of going to Abbotsford. tsn.ca ↗

The last 14 days of NHL news, from team, league and reporter sources, in our own words. Not confirmed by the team means a reporter or outlet has it but the team (or the league) hasn't said so yet. Stories aren't edited after they're posted: when one is confirmed later, or turns out to be wrong, a note goes under it.

CBJ 4–3 PHI OT

Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ5-5-0 · 10 pts15 shots
4
Final/OTXfinity Mobile Arena
3
Philadelphia FlyersPHI3-7-4 · 10 pts31 shots
1st2nd3rdOTTCBJ30014PHI01203

Puckline's Report

Columbus scored three goals in 2:46 of the first period, then spent the next 40 minutes trying to give them back, and the Flyers almost took the gift. Adam Fantilli, Kent Johnson and Denton Mateychuk built the 3-0 lead on a Dan Vladar who finished with 11 saves on 15 shots, which is a lot of goals for a team that only managed 15 shots all night. Noah Cates and Trevor Zegras chipped away, and Jamie Drysdale tied it with the goalie pulled and 11 seconds left. Then Johnson, with two goals and an assist, ended it 2:22 into overtime. Cam Talbot made 28 saves for the Blue Jackets. Philadelphia outshot Columbus 31-15 and still lost, now 0-3 in 3-on-3 overtime, the hockey version of running a marathon and missing the finish line by a step. The Flyers keep finding new ways to lose, and they're getting creative about it.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

The Bruins scored 91 seconds in, on a Pavel Zacha power-play goal, and then apparently decided that was plenty. Boston managed 15 shots all night. Carolina had 30, and Jeremy Swayman (28 saves) kept it close until the Hurricanes finally solved him. Jackson Blake tied it with 52 seconds left in the first, and Sebastian Aho put home his eighth of the season at 10:19 of the third for the winner. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 14 saves, which is basically a paid night off. Nicolas Deslauriers and Tanner Jeannot dropped the gloves in the first for the evening's other entertainment, and Mark Jankowski returned to the Carolina lineup. The Hurricanes move to 10-2-2. The Bruins are 9-3-1 and still good, but 15 shots against a top team is a business trip where you forget your laptop.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline's Report

Chicago snapped a three-game losing streak, and it took a defenseman scoring his first of the year to do it. Samuel Helenius gave the Kings an early lead with his first goal of the season at 2:31, and Los Angeles then went the final 57 minutes without another one. Roman Kantserov tied it on a second-period power play off a Connor Bedard feed, and Wyatt Kaiser won it at 7:17 of the third, from Frank Nazar and Patrick Kane. Spencer Knight was excellent with 25 saves on 26 shots; Anton Forsberg made 25 at the other end. Quinton Byfield fired six shots and Artemi Panarin played nearly 24 minutes without a point. The Blackhawks improve to 4-8-0. The Kings fall to 3-6-2 with one goal from their fourth line and none from anybody paid to score them.

2
FinalEnterprise Center

St Louis BluesSTL5-6-1 · 11 pts46 shots
1st2nd3rdTMTL0112STL0000

Puckline's Report

Jacob Fowler stopped all 46 shots the Blues threw at him, and St. Louis threw just about everything, the rink's spare pucks included. Philip Broberg had six shots, four other Blues had five each, and none of them got one past Fowler. The Canadiens needed only 20 shots of their own. Zachary Bolduc scored in the second period, Florian Xhekaj got his first of the season early in the third, and Mike Matheson assisted on both. Jordan Binnington made 18 saves and still took the loss, which won't help a goalie already sitting on the trade boards. Montreal is 7-3-2. The Blues fall to 5-6-1 after outshooting a team 46-20 and getting shut out, and at some point they have to stop blaming the goalie and start blaming the aim.

Puckline's Report

The Islanders led 3-0 eight minutes into the second period, and Nashville spent the rest of regulation proving that no lead in Music City is safe. Anthony Duclair, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat built it; Filip Forsberg (power play), Alexander Kerfoot and Ryan O'Reilly erased it, O'Reilly tying the game 4:16 into the third. Overtime solved nothing, though Matthew Schaefer played all of it and finished with 32:16 of ice time, the kind of workload usually reserved for a veteran. In the shootout Kyle Palmieri and Horvat scored, while O'Reilly and Forsberg both missed. Semyon Varlamov made 20 saves; Juuse Saros made 25. New York is 6-4-2. The Predators are 4-3-5, a team so committed to the loser point it should hang a banner for it.

Puckline's Report

Connor Hellebuyck's Devils debut was about as stressful as a warm bath: 17 saves on 18 shots, with the skaters in front of him doing everything else. Nico Hischier scored twice, opening the night at 2:41 and adding another 38 seconds into the second. Jesper Boqvist, Luke Hughes and Jack Hughes did the rest, and the Hughes brothers each had a goal. Justin Hryckowian got Dallas its only goal. Jamie Benn and Brenden Dillon fought in the second period, which was the closest the Stars came to winning anything. Casey DeSmith allowed five goals on 27 shots. New Jersey has won four straight and is 8-4-0. Dallas falls to 7-4-1 and looked like a team that had read about Hellebuyck all week and decided not to bother him.

Puckline's Report

Florida was up 3-0 before the 11-minute mark, and Winnipeg's penalty kill treated the Panthers' power play like a guest of honour. Carter Verhaeghe scored twice on the power play, Niko Mikkola added one in between, and Sam Reinhart made it three power-play goals on the night in the second. Brady Tkachuk finished it in the third, with brother Matthew assisting for his fourth helper of the night. Seth Jones had three assists. Adam Lowry's shorthanded goal was the only thing Jets fans got to cheer. Akira Schmid made 24 saves; Clay Stevenson allowed five on 24 shots. The Panthers are 7-4-2. The Jets are 4-5-3, and a penalty kill that leaky makes every Florida trip to the box look like a free shift.

Puckline's Report

Three fights and two power-play goals: the Wild brought both the fists and the finish to Utah. Liam O'Brien and Michael McCarron fought in the first, Mikhail Sergachev and Matt Boldy went 88 seconds later, and Vincent Trocheck and Danila Yurov added a third in the second. When the hockey broke out, Minnesota's power play did the damage. Joel Eriksson Ek scored in the second and Kirill Kaprizov got his 14th of the season 48 seconds into the third, both with Quinn Hughes assisting. Maxim Shabanov made it 3-0, and Logan Cooley's late 6-on-5 goal only spoiled the shutout. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves; Karel Vejmelka made 27. The Wild are 9-3-2. Utah is 8-5-0 and learned that winning the fights doesn't count on the scoreboard.

Puckline's Report

For almost 40 minutes nobody scored; then Vegas remembered it's the house. Braeden Bowman scored on the power play with 11 seconds left in the second, Shane Pinto answered on a power play 34 seconds into the third, and Raphael Lavoie scored his first of the season at 8:01 for the winner. William Karlsson and Jack Eichel then added empty-netters, which turns a nervy 2-1 into a 4-1 final. Adin Hill was sharp with 25 saves on 26 shots, and Jonas Johansson matched him with 25 of 27 before the empty net did the rest. Mitch Marner had an assist on Karlsson's goal. Vegas is 9-4-1. The Senators fall to 8-5-0 and flew all that way to learn the Vegas lesson: you can stay at the table a long time, but you don't walk out ahead.

Puckline's Report

The Canucks hadn't won in double-digit games, trailed 5-2 with under eight minutes left, and somehow won. Anaheim had this one framed: A.J. Greer scored twice, Jeff Malott, Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson piled on, and it was 4-1 after two. Then Brock Boeser and Jamie Oleksiak scored, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki scored twice with the goalie pulled, at 17:14 and 18:03, to tie it. Filip Hronek won it on a power play 4:49 into overtime, his first of the season. Lukas Dostal allowed six on 33 shots; Leevi Meriläinen gave up five on 23 and still got the win. Vancouver is 3-10-1. The Ducks are 5-6-1 and found the one way to lose to a team that had forgotten how to win: give up four goals in the last 12 minutes of hockey.

Puckline's Report

Yaroslav Askarov stopped 38 of 39 shots and lost, which is the San Jose experience in one sentence. Olen Zellweger scored 50 seconds into the second period, and that was the only puck anybody got past Askarov all night. Zach Benson's first of the season went into an empty net with 55 seconds left. At the other end Colten Ellis was barely needed and perfect when he was, stopping all 23 shots for the shutout. Owen Power assisted on both Buffalo goals. The Sabres improve to 5-4-3. The Sharks fall to 6-6-1 after getting outshot 39-23 at home, and a rebuild that leaves its best player stopping 38 shots alone is a rebuild that still has a long way to go.

PHI @ WSH · 7:30 PM ET

Philadelphia FlyersPHI3-7-4 · 10 PTSML +190
@7:30 PM ETWed Oct 28 · Capital One Arena
PHI +190MLWSH -235
Washington CapitalsWSH6-4-0 · 12 PTSML -235

Puckline Preview

The Flyers roll into Washington on the second night of a back-to-back, still buzzing from a comeback that went nowhere: down 3-0 to Columbus on Tuesday, Jamie Drysdale tied it with 11 seconds left, and Kent Johnson ended it in overtime. Philadelphia is now 0-3 in 3-on-3 overtime, 3-7-4 overall, and dead last in the league at 1.93 goals a game, which is the kind of offense that makes a 6.5 total look like a dare. Per the Flyers' own preview, they're still hunting their first win over a Metropolitan team. Trevor Zegras is the one guy lighting it up, with 12 points and nine in his last five. Travis Konecny and Owen Tippett remain on IR, and Joseph Woll is projected in goal.

The Capitals, meanwhile, have played once in seven days and are 5-2 at home. Logan Thompson was the first goalie off the ice at Wednesday's morning skate and is projected to start, though Spencer Carbery would only say "We'll see," and Jack St. Ivany, the waiver claim from Winnipeg, looks set for his Caps debut on a pair with Cole Hutson. Alex Ovechkin is skating on the third line these days, which is a sentence nobody thought they'd read. Rested team against a tired one that can't score: the Flyers will need Zegras to be a one-man fire department again.

By Puckline Prince

CGY @ EDM · 8:30 PM ET

Calgary FlamesCGY5-6-0 · 10 PTSML +176
@8:30 PM ETWed Oct 28 · Rogers Place
CGY +176MLEDM -215
Edmonton OilersEDM8-2-2 · 18 PTSML -215

Puckline Preview

The first Battle of Alberta of the season, and the Flames show up as the hotter team, which is not a phrase Oilers fans enjoy. Calgary has won four straight, its power play has scored in five straight games and its penalty kill has killed 11 in a row, per the Flames. Devin Cooley, named the NHL's Second Star of the Week, is projected again after outplaying Sergei Bobrovsky in Monday's 5-2 win over Toronto. Calgary also took three of four from Edmonton last season. The catch: the Flames are 28th in scoring and 31st in goals allowed, so the streak has been held together with tape.

Edmonton is 8-2-2 and first in the league in goals (4.33 a game) and power play (35%). Connor McDavid has 34 points and a point in all 12 games, and Leon Draisaitl has 12 goals. The defense is another story: 28th in goals against and a 26th-ranked penalty kill, and the Oilers have dropped two straight at home for the first time this season, 7-2 to Toronto and in a shootout to Detroit. Mattias Ekholm is back on the top pair, Zach Hyman is out, and Tristan Jarry (.869) is projected with Devon Levi on IR. Edmonton's power play against Calgary's streaking kill is the matchup to watch.

By Puckline Prince

NJD @ COL · 9:00 PM ET

New Jersey DevilsNJD8-4-0 · 16 PTSML +146
@9:00 PM ETWed Oct 28 · Ball Arena
NJD +146MLCOL -178
Colorado AvalancheCOL6-5-1 · 13 PTSML -178

Puckline Preview

Eight days after these two last met, the Devils come to Denver on a four-game winning streak, every one in regulation, outscoring teams 16-6, per New Jersey Hockey Now. Connor Hellebuyck stopped 17 of 18 in his Devils debut in Dallas on Tuesday and gets the night off, so Jake Allen starts the back half of the back-to-back. Allen made 31 saves when New Jersey beat Colorado 4-3 on Oct. 20, a game the Avs nearly stole back when Artturi Lehkonen scored twice in the last 3:13. Declan Chisholm, who scored in that one, rotates back in on defense. Nico Hischier, with two goals in Dallas, is three points from 500 for his career.

Colorado is 6-5-1 and coming off a 6-2 beating in Nashville, with Jared Bednar publicly wondering why a veteran group needs a push to show up. The Avs score plenty (4.08 a game, 2nd) and give it back (22nd in goals against). Nicolas Roy returns as the second-line center, Nazem Kadri slides to the third line, and Mackenzie Blackwood is projected in goal. Lehkonen leads the team with 10 goals, and Chris Johnston reports his extension talks are not close. Rested Avs against road-weary Devils: we find out tonight whether anybody in that room was listening to Bednar.

By Puckline Prince

TOR @ SEA · 10:00 PM ET

Toronto Maple LeafsTOR7-5-2 · 16 PTSML -120
@10:00 PM ETWed Oct 28 · Climate Pledge Arena
TOR -120MLSEA +100
Seattle KrakenSEA7-4-1 · 15 PTSML +100

Puckline Preview

Bobby McMann gets his first crack at the team that traded him at last season's deadline, and Seattle is making a show of it: the Kraken's projected lines bump him to the top line with Matty Beniers and Jordan Eberle. McMann is also 2-for-2 in shootouts this season, so Toronto might want to settle this in 65 minutes. The Kraken (7-4-1) swept last season's series, including a 4-3 overtime win in Toronto. Jared McCann is out about 10 weeks, Jani Nyman (nine goals in nine AHL games) takes his spot, and Philipp Grubauer is projected in goal.

The Leafs are 7-5-2 and coming off a 5-2 loss in Calgary, the night Auston Matthews reached 800 points. Kirill Marchenko left that game with a lower-body injury and is questionable; the team is due to update his status at the morning skate. John Tavares and Chris Tanev remain out, and Anthony Stolarz (4-1-0) is expected to start after Bobrovsky's rough night. Toronto's penalty kill is the best in the league at 93.6%, while Seattle's sits 26th at 70.6% against a top-five Leafs power play. Seattle will have to stay out of the box, or this one gets out of hand fast.

By Puckline Prince
